Original images are not bundled. Only approved selected examples are compressed and published; all other attempts remain audit records.

images.prompt: Natural food photograph of one whole red bell pepper standing upright on a pale stone kitchen counter, its short green stem leaning left. A single detached green leaf lies behind and right. Soft daylight from a side window, warm gray wall, low three-quarter camera, fresh natural texture. Vertical 4:5, 1024x1280. Full objects visible with breathing room. Natural photography, realistic materials and lighting; no text, logo, watermark, or illustration.

review.reason: Independent inspection confirms one complete red pepper with a single attached curved stem and one separate leaf at right. Lobes, leaf veins, water drops, counter contact and window lighting are photographic and coherent; no marks or labels.

images.actual_source_analysis: One glossy red bell pepper stands upright slightly left of center on a pale stone countertop. Its body has rounded vertical lobes and a single green stem curving upward and toward the left, with one pale cut end. Small water droplets cover the skin. One detached green leaf lies behind and to the right, its stem pointing left and pointed tip toward the lower right. Both the pepper and leaf are fully visible. A window at upper left provides daylight, casting shadows to the lower right against a warm gray wall.

images.prompt:
Hand-hammered copper sheet with shallow irregular dimples and modest warm oxidation in surface recesses.
Preserve: Subject count, outer silhouette, openings, attachments, and contact points. Source camera viewpoint, framing, relative scale, and placement. Recognizable subject identity and existing background structure.
Recast existing solid surfaces as hand-hammered copper, preserving original contours, protrusions, component boundaries, and attachment relationships.
Use warm copper, dark reddish-brown recesses, and small pale metallic highlights; avoid broad turquoise patina.
Keep structural grooves and boundaries from the source; express edges through changing metallic reflection rather than outlines.
Cover surfaces with shallow irregular hammer dimples scaled to the object, with slightly darker recesses.
Retain the light direction; each dimple catches a restrained highlight while larger reflections describe the overall form.
Preserve framing, subject count, scale, orientation, placement, and support shadows.
Wrap hammer marks with the local surface curvature and reduce their scale near fine details.
Finish as worked copper with subtle oxidation, avoiding crumpled foil, carved decoration, or added hardware.
Change existing solid surfaces and their material response only; retain parts, silhouettes, openings, and placement.
Use the supplied photograph as the sole composition reference. Keep the entire source frame, original 4:5 aspect ratio, camera viewpoint, subject scale, and all margins. Produce at least 1024x1280 pixels. Output only the finished image.
Avoid: Turquoise corrosion covering the subject, carved motifs, or new rivets. Crumpled foil, deep dents that alter shape, or melted edges. Extra stems, duplicated leaves, text, logos, or watermarks.

review.reason: Independent comparison confirms one pepper, one stem and one leaf retain their outlines, positions and fine structure. Shallow irregular copper hammer dimples follow curvature, with warm metallic highlights and restrained darker recesses. The counter and window frame are also converted, which the recipe permits for existing solid surfaces; their structure and illumination remain intact. No new rivets, ornaments or deep shape-changing dents.
